programme.notes: Programme as recorded in the merged KB (Bachelor of Advanced Computing; not re-researched in this top-up). The Australian academic year 2027 starts with Semester 1 (February 2027), the first intake of that year.

scholarship_exists.quote: To be eligible for this award, you must: be an international student hold citizenship in one of the countries or regions listed below receive admission into a full-time undergraduate coursework or postgraduate coursework degree, commencing in 2027*
scholarship_exists.notes: Same page: 'Recipients will be awarded a University contribution of 20 percent of their tuition fee for the duration of their course' and 'The Award is applicable to new commencements in 2027.' PARTIAL (20% of tuition, applied to the offer; no cash, no living costs). Citizenship-restricted: only the listed countries/regions (Africa, Central Asia incl. Kazakhstan, South/Southeast Asia, Japan, Mongolia, South Korea, Lebanon, Turkey, Eastern Europe, South and Central America). Applied for with a personal statement (3 x 200 words) during the admission application; excluded: MBA, EMBA, study abroad, executive education, distance mode, Law Dual Degree pathway. This replaces the base draft's Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship, whose quote was never verified (the International Guide PDF is too large for the evidence reader, and the scheme page https://www.sydney.edu.au/scholarships/e/vice-chancellor-international-scholarships-scheme.html renders its body client-side: 759 readable characters, no award text).

scholarship_international.quote: To be eligible for this award, you must: be an international student hold citizenship in one of the countries or regions listed below receive admission into a full-time undergraduate coursework or postgraduate coursework degree, commencing in 2027*
scholarship_international.notes: International students are the eligible group, but only citizens of the listed countries/regions; an applicant from an unlisted country is not eligible. Terms on the same page: 'Applicants must hold citizenship of one of the countries listed as eligible for the Award. Proof of residency will be required.'
